recipe-section-1.markdown:

- **All-purpose flour** : 10 g ( [**0.34**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=34s) )
- **Milk** (your choice): 120 g ( [**0:34**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=34s) )

• Strong flour (bread flour) : 50 g ( 0:34 )
  • All-purpose flour : 10 g ( 0.34 )
  • Milk (your choice): 120 g ( 0:34 )
recipe-section-1.title: For the Tangzhong (starter paste):

recipe-section-2.html: • Egg : 1 beaten egg ( 15:06 )
recipe-section-2.title: For the gilding:

recipe-section-4.markdown:
- In a small saucepan, mix the 50 g of strong flour, the 10 g of regular flour and the 120 g of milk ( [**0:34**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=34s) ) .
- Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until a thick paste/glue consistency is achieved ( [**0:19**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=19s) ) . Let cool.
recipe-section-4.html:
• In a small saucepan, mix the 50 g of strong flour, the 10 g of regular flour and the 120 g of milk ( 0:34 ) .
  • Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until a thick paste/glue consistency is achieved ( 0:19 ) . Let cool.
recipe-section-4.title: Step 1: Tangzhong Preparation

recipe-section-5.markdown:
- In the bowl of your stand mixer, break the 8 eggs ( [**1:08**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=68s) ) .
- Add the salt (13 g) ( [**1:18**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=78s) ) , the cooled Tangzhong ( [**0:19**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=19s) ) , the strong flour (500 g) ( [**2:46**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=166s) ) and the classic flour (90 g) ( [**4:33**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=273s) ) .
- Add the dry yeast (14 g) ( [**5:19**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=319s) ) , the milk (80 g) ( [**5:27**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=327s) ) and the sugar (200 g) ( [**7:01**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=421s) ) .
- Using the dough hook, start mixing slowly (speed 3 on a KitchenAid) ( [**7:38**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=458s) ) .
- Let the robot run for **10 to 15 minutes** until the dough begins to homogenize and form an elastic gluten network ( [**7:50**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=470s) ) .
recipe-section-5.html:
• In the bowl of your stand mixer, break the 8 eggs ( 1:08 ) .
  • Add the salt (13 g) ( 1:18 ) , the cooled Tangzhong ( 0:19 ) , the strong flour (500 g) ( 2:46 ) and the classic flour (90 g) ( 4:33 ) .
  • Add the dry yeast (14 g) ( 5:19 ) , the milk (80 g) ( 5:27 ) and the sugar (200 g) ( 7:01 ) .
  • Using the dough hook, start mixing slowly (speed 3 on a KitchenAid) ( 7:38 ) .
  • Let the robot run for 10 to 15 minutes until the dough begins to homogenize and form an elastic gluten network ( 7:50 ) .
recipe-section-5.title: Step 2: Mixing the main dough

recipe-section-6.markdown:
- While the mixer is running, gradually incorporate the softened butter, piece by piece ( [**8:14**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=494s) ) . Wait until each piece is fully incorporated before adding the next ( [**8:27**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=507s) ) .
- Once all the butter has been incorporated, cover the bowl with plastic wrap ( [**9:05**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=545s) ) .
- Let the dough rest and rise at room temperature for **2 hours** ( [**8:57**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=537s) ) .
recipe-section-6.html:
• While the mixer is running, gradually incorporate the softened butter, piece by piece ( 8:14 ) . Wait until each piece is fully incorporated before adding the next ( 8:27 ) .
  • Once all the butter has been incorporated, cover the bowl with plastic wrap ( 9:05 ) .
  • Let the dough rest and rise at room temperature for 2 hours ( 8:57 ) .
recipe-section-6.title: 3. Incorporating the butter and the first rise
recipe-section-6.heading_html: 3. Incorporating the butter and the first rise

recipe-section-7.markdown:
- Lightly oil your work surface or pastry mat ( [**9:31**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=571s) ) .
- Deflate the dough by lifting and firmly folding it over several times ( [**10:29**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=629s) ) . Brioche dough is very sticky, this is perfectly normal ( [**10:19**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=619s) ) . Sprinkle with a little all-purpose flour if it is too difficult to handle ( [**11:28**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=688s) ) .
- Using a pastry cutter, divide the dough in two (to make two cake tins) ( [**1:25**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=85s) ) .
- Next, divide each half into several pieces ( [**12:55**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=775s) ) . Form balls of different sizes with the palm of your hand using a circular motion ( [**13:20**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=800s) ) .
- Place the balls of dough side by side in your cake tins ( [**12:35**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=755s) ) .
recipe-section-7.html:
• Lightly oil your work surface or pastry mat ( 9:31 ) .
  • Deflate the dough by lifting and firmly folding it over several times ( 10:29 ) . Brioche dough is very sticky, this is perfectly normal ( 10:19 ) . Sprinkle with a little all-purpose flour if it is too difficult to handle ( 11:28 ) .
  • Using a pastry cutter, divide the dough in two (to make two cake tins) ( 1:25 ) .
  • Next, divide each half into several pieces ( 12:55 ) . Form balls of different sizes with the palm of your hand using a circular motion ( 13:20 ) .
  • Place the balls of dough side by side in your cake tins ( 12:35 ) .
recipe-section-7.title: Step 4: Shaping the balls

recipe-section-8.markdown:
- Preheat your oven to **160 °C** ( [**14:56**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=896s) ) .
- Generously brush the tops of your brioches with the beaten egg to obtain a beautiful golden crust ( [**15:06**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=906s) ) .
- Place in the oven and let it cook for approximately **25 minutes** ( [**15:16**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=916s) ) .
- Allow to cool slightly before slicing or enjoying in detachable pieces ( [**13:34**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axvT9XXz1KQ&t=814s) ) .
recipe-section-8.html:
• Preheat your oven to 160 °C ( 14:56 ) .
  • Generously brush the tops of your brioches with the beaten egg to obtain a beautiful golden crust ( 15:06 ) .
  • Place in the oven and let it cook for approximately 25 minutes ( 15:16 ) .
  • Allow to cool slightly before slicing or enjoying in detachable pieces ( 13:34 ) .
recipe-section-8.title: Step 5: Cooking
